title: Meta Ads Audit Cost: Free Offers, Quotes and Price Drivers
summary: What a Meta ads audit costs in 2026: free agency audits, a $300 freelancer starting price, private quotes, and the scope that moves the total.
body_markdown:
A Meta ads audit can cost nothing, a few hundred dollars, or a private quote, depending on who runs it and what you get back. Agencies often give a free audit as the first step of a sales process, while freelancers sell a fixed-price review with a call. If the audit shows you need more finished ads rather than cleaner settings, Knowlify is our top pick for that next step: done-for-you AI video ads, with plans starting at $5,000 a month.


Knowlify publishes this guide and is the service we recommend for finished ads. Its services are finished ads and Meta campaign management, so price any audit separately from a creative quote.


## What do Meta ads audits cost in practice?


Few providers publish a standalone audit price. The table shows each offer as the provider describes it, checked in October 2026, and it includes the one fixed price we could confirm on a freelancer's own page.


Provider Audit offer Published price What the offer includes


[Brighter Click](https://www.brighterclick.com/facebook-ads-agency) Every engagement starts with a free audit Free audit; management pricing not published Facebook and Instagram campaign management


[inBeat](https://inbeat.agency/meta-advertising-agency) Free audit offered Not published Meta campaign management with pixel and Conversions API setup


[Disruptive Advertising](https://disruptiveadvertising.com/social-media-advertising/) Free audit as the first of three tiers Free audit; strategy tier at "a couple thousand dollars" A Do It With Us strategy tier and a done-for-you tier


[KlientBoost](https://www.klientboost.com/services/facebook-ads-agency/) One-time ad audit among five engagement options Not published Audit, setup, consulting, ongoing management or a revenue partnership


[Freelancer on Contra](https://contra.com/s/FYqZ6ZeX-facebook-ad-account-audit-explanatory-session) Facebook ad account audit with an explanatory session Starting at $300 About a week of review, a 15 to 30 minute intake call and a recorded 60-minute results call


A free audit is a sales step, so ask what you keep. Does the review end with a written list of findings, or with a proposal to hire the agency? Compare a free review with a paid one only when both produce the same written output.


## Why do audit prices differ so much?


Scope does most of the work. The freelancer listing covers the ad account, its history and the wider digital marketing presence and funnel, which is broader than a settings check on Meta alone. A review limited to campaign structure, pixel events and budgets takes less of an auditor's time than one that also reviews landing pages and creative results.


Four other inputs move the price: the number of ad accounts and active campaigns, the access you grant, whether the output is a written report or a call, and whether the reviewer makes the fixes. Ask each provider to state all four in writing before you compare totals.


## What should a Meta ads audit check?


Start with tracking. Meta describes its[Conversions API](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/conversions-api) as a connection between your server, website platform, app or CRM and its systems, used to optimize targeting, lower cost per result and measure outcomes. An audit should name who set up those events and who fixes them when they stop arriving.


Next, check whether campaigns can leave the learning phase. Meta says delivery usually stabilizes after about 50 results in the week after an ad set's last significant edit, according to its[learning phase guidance](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/112167992830700) . An account that is edited often, or split across many small ad sets, may never collect enough results to settle, so a review should flag that before it recommends more spend.


Then check budgets. Meta sets[minimum budgets](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/203183363050448) that vary by country and objective, and Ads Manager shows an alert when a budget falls below the minimum. For a cost-per-result goal, Meta advises a daily budget of at least five times that goal. A review that skips this check can recommend a spend level the account cannot use. Our[Facebook ad agency pricing guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/facebook-ad-agency-pricing) explains how fees and budgets interact.


Creative supply is the last check. Meta's engineering post on its[Andromeda retrieval system](https://engineering.fb.com/2024/12/02/production-engineering/meta-andromeda-advantage-automation-next-gen-personalized-ads-retrieval-engine/) says the number of ad creatives in its recommendation systems is expected to grow significantly. Count distinct concepts, not files: five cut-downs of one idea are one concept, and a reviewer should say so in the findings.


[Clicks Geek's public audit guide](https://clicksgeek.com/facebook-ads-audit/) covers a similar list: campaign structure, targeting, creative performance, pixel and conversion tracking, and placements and budget, with a prioritized action plan as its last step. A provider that cannot name its checks in writing cannot scope a price for you.
